parole.significato: Of or relating to the Ahmadiyya Muslim Jama'at (a religious movement based on Sunni Islam).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَحْمَدِيّ (ʔaḥmadiyy) or Persian احمدی. By surface analysis, Ahmad + -i.

parole.significato: Any of a variety of Middle Eastern biscuits and baked goods, usually sweet.
parole.testo: From Arabic كَعْك (kaʕk, “biscuit, cookie”) and Persian کاک (“biscuit, cookie, cake”). Likely a distant cognate with cake.

parole.significato: Synonym of caravanserai (particularly in Middle Eastern contexts)
parole.testo: From Arabic خَان (ḵān, “inn, caravanserai, hotel”) and Persian خان (xân, “inn, caravanserai”).

parole.significato: Various forms of covered animal-borne litters, chiefly for female passengers.
parole.testo: From Arabic مِحَفَّة (miḥaffa) directly and via Persian محافه (miḥâfah), Urdu محفہ (miḥaffa), and Hindi मिहफ़्फ़ा (mihaffā), related to Arabic حَفَّ (ḥaffa, “to enclose, to border”).

parole.significato: crude native borax, formerly imported from Tibet, and once the chief source of boric compounds
parole.testo: From Arabic تِنْكَار (tinkār), from Persian تنکار (tankâr), from Sanskrit टांकण (ṭāṃkaṇa). Compare altincar and tincar.

parole.significato: One of the Bantu-speaking inhabitants of this part of East Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic زَنْج (zanj, “The East African coastlands”), from Persian زنگ (zang, “East Africa”) or its Middle Persian etymon; see the Persian entry for more.
From Arabic [script needed] (zerdawā), probably of Persian origin; compare Persian زرد (zard, “yellow”) and the dialectal suffix و (-ow, -aw) that creates nouns from adjectives.
